html:
Zaatari is a refugee camp in the desert of northern Jordan, near the Syrian border, opened in July 2012 for people fleeing the Syrian civil war. At its peak it was one of the largest refugee camps in the world.

Tents gave way to metal cabins, and the camp grew a main street of shops, nicknamed the Champs-Élysées, with bakeries, barbers and wedding dress shops. Most of its people come from the nearby Syrian province of Daraa.

Jordan has taken in hundreds of thousands of Syrians, most of them living in towns rather than camps, a heavy load on a country short of water. See also the Syrian refugee crisis and Palestinian refugees.
